### Risks from a model trained on a case-control sample (`case_control_risks`)

- **Slot:** the model; place in it 1.6.
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself. Learns the case share of the rows the model is trained on, so under Predict it is fitted inside each training fold with the model; the stated population prevalence is a number the person gives, not learned from any row.
- **Needs:**
  - a classifier trained on an unmatched or frequency-matched case-control sample
  - the population prevalence of the outcome (one per matching stratum under frequency matching)
- **Question:** How do the model's predictions become risks?
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the CASECONTROL package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prior_correction`: Recalibrated to the population prevalence (prior correction) | King & Zeng 2001's prior correction; Prentice & Pyke 1979 for why only the intercept moves | Sound when cases and controls were drawn by the outcome alone (or per matching stratum, with each stratum's prevalence) and the prevalence is known | recommended, 1 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: a case-control sample gives no absolute risk there; its odds ratios are its effects | not offered, 1 |
| `ranking_only`: No risks: how well the model separates cases from controls | The case-control sample's own probabilities are not risks (Rothman, Greenland & Lash, Modern Epidemiology, ch. 8) | Sound without the prevalence; under frequency matching the matching factors' share of the ranking is understated (Janes & Pepe 2008) | available, 2 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: a case-control sample gives no absolute risk there; its odds ratios are its effects | not offered, 2 |
| `within_set_ranking`: Rank each case against its own matched controls | The conditional model's linear predictor within each set (Breslow & Day 1980; Janes & Pepe 2008) | Sound for individually matched sets, the only ranking they support | available, 3 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: a case-control sample gives no absolute risk there; its odds ratios are its effects | not offered, 3 |

**Ranked by the data:** the app offers these options in another order than the rank above where the data decide it; what it offers first under each condition:

- Under prediction, an unmatched case-control sample, with the population prevalence stated: `prior_correction`: Risks recalibrated to the population prevalence (prior correction), the correction learned in each training fold.
- Under prediction, an unmatched case-control sample, with no population prevalence: `ranking_only`: How well the model separates cases from controls; it gives no risks.
- Under prediction, a frequency-matched case-control sample, with the prevalence stated within each matching stratum: `prior_correction`: Risks recalibrated to the population prevalence within each matching stratum (prior correction), the correction learned in each training fold.
- Under prediction, a frequency-matched case-control sample, with one prevalence for every stratum: `ranking_only`: How well the model separates cases from controls; it gives no risks. The controls were matched to the cases on some factors, so how well those factors separate cases from controls here understates it in the population (Janes & Pepe 2008).
- Under prediction, individually matched sets, with or without a prevalence: `within_set_ranking`: Each case ranked against its own matched controls, by the conditional model fitted in each training fold.

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. in each training fold, fit the model
2. learn that fold's case share
3. shift each held-out prediction's log odds by the sample's odds over the population's
4. report risks (or, without the prevalence, the ranking only)

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:risks_sentence`: The methods sentence of recalibrated risks under Predict.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| conflicts | `no_risk_from_matched_sets` (id `matched_risk_refused`) | `prior_correction`; when individually matched sets | prediction | risks for individually matched sets are refused: the conditional model has no baseline risk, and matched controls are no random sample of non-cases *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: rank each case against its own matched controls; odds ratios. | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:eligible` |
| conflicts | `prevalence_needed` (id `needs_prevalence`) | `prior_correction`; when no population prevalence stated | prediction | risks without the population prevalence are refused *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: give the population prevalence; the ranking only. | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:eligible` |
| conflicts | `prevalence_per_stratum` (id `stratum_prevalence`) | `prior_correction`; when frequency matching with a single prevalence | prediction | one prevalence under frequency matching is refused: the controls' sampling differs by stratum *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: the prevalence within each matching stratum; the ranking only. | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:eligible` |
| implies | `offset_in_fold` (id `fold_share`) | `prior_correction`; when always | prediction | the case share that sets the offset is learned from each training fold | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:PriorCorrected` |
| implies | `sets_whole_in_folds` (id `sets_whole`) | any option; when a matched-set column | prediction | matched sets (and sets sharing a person) stay whole inside folds | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:case_control_folds` |
| conflicts | `weights_correct_twice` (id `no_weights`) | `prior_correction`; when a survey design | prediction | survey weights beside the prior correction are refused: both would correct the sampling *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: recalibrate without the survey weights; the ranking only. | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:predicted_risks` |
| conflicts | `risks_not_under_estimate` (id `estimate_refused`) | any option; when the Estimate an effect goal | inference | not offered under Estimate an effect: no absolute risk from a case-control sample *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: odds ratios. | `turbotab.core.methods.case_control:eligible` |

**Primary sources:**

- King & Zeng 2001, Polit Anal 9:137
- Prentice & Pyke 1979, Biometrika 66:403
- Janes & Pepe 2008, Biometrics 64:1
- Breslow & Day 1980, IARC Sci Publ 32, ch. 6 and 7
- Rothman, Greenland & Lash, Modern Epidemiology, ch. 8

### Diagnostics of the primary model (`diagnostics`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** descriptive: may read every row to say whether the data are corrupted, but informs no modeling choice. reads every analyzed row to report; changes nothing until a response is recorded
- **Needs:**
  - a fitted primary model
- **Question:** stated
- **Where:** recorded by `respond_diagnostic`; run by the `effects` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference blocked until recorded.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the ESTIMAND package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keep_labeled`: Keep the estimate, labeled with the failed check | customary: the check reported beside the estimate | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 1 | Sound when the failure is stated with the estimate | available, 2 |
| `period_hazard_ratios`: The hazard ratio before and after the median event time | customary for a proportional-hazards failure (Grambsch & Therneau 1994) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 2 | Sound: the ratio is shown where it holds | recommended, 1 |
| `without_influential`: The primary refit without the influential rows, beside | customary for influential rows (Cook 1977) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 3 | Sound as a sensitivity analysis beside the primary, never in its place | available, 3 |

**Ranked by the data:** the app offers these options in another order than the rank above where the data decide it; what it offers first under each condition:

- Under inference, a failed proportional-hazards check (a Cox fit): `period_hazard_ratios`: the exposure's hazard ratio before and after the median event time, beside the average over follow-up
- Under inference, a failed influence check (Cook's distance): `without_influential`: the primary model refit without the influential rows, beside it
- Under inference, no check failed: nothing is asked: the checks are reported beside the estimate

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. the primary fit
2. the check
3. the reading
4. the recorded response

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.stages.effects:methods_sentence`: The methods text this stage writes, from what it fitted: the sequence, the display rule, the marginal standardization, the diagnostics and their responses, and the sensitivity analyses.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `a recorded response` (id `failed-check-recorded`) | any option; when a failed check of the exposure | inference | the check carries respond_diagnostic exits; the response recorded is shown and stated, never applied silently |  |
| enables | `the period hazard ratios` (id `ph-period-ratios`) | any option; when a failed proportional-hazards check, the period response recorded | inference | the hazard ratio before and after the median event time is shown |  |
| enables | `the refit without influential rows` (id `influence-refit`) | any option; when a failed influence check, that response recorded | inference | the primary refit without the flagged rows is shown beside |  |

**Primary sources:**

- Grambsch & Therneau 1994, Biometrika 81:515
- Cook 1977, Technometrics 19:15

### The E-value of a difference, standardized by the estimand's SD (`evalue_sd`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** descriptive: may read every row to say whether the data are corrupted, but informs no modeling choice. reads the analyzed rows' outcome (and their survey weights) to standardize the reported estimate; informs no modeling choice
- **Needs:**
  - a reported difference
  - the survey answer
- **Question:** stated
- **Where:** run by the `effects` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 14.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference recommended.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the LEASH package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design_weighted`: The surveyed population's SD | uncommon (most reports use the sample SD) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect | not offered, 1 | Sound under the surveyed-population answer: the estimate is the population's | recommended, 1 |
| `sample`: The analyzed rows' SD | customary (EValue::evalues.OLS's sd) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect | not offered, 2 | Sound under the sample answer | available, 2 |

**Ranked by the data:** the app offers these options in another order than the rank above where the data decide it; what it offers first under each condition:

- Under inference, the surveyed-population answer (the analysis weights): `design_weighted`: the surveyed population's SD
- Under inference, the sample answer (no weights): `sample`: the analyzed rows' SD

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. the reported difference
2. the outcome's SD the estimand speaks of
3. d = estimate / SD
4. RR ≈ exp(0.91 d), and its E-value

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.stages.effects:methods_sentence`: The methods text this stage writes, from what it fitted: the sequence, the display rule, the marginal standardization, the diagnostics and their responses, and the sensitivity analyses.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `the design-weighted SD` (id `evalue-population-sd`) | any option; when the surveyed-population answer and a design-based difference | inference | the effects stage and the causal lane standardize the difference by the outcome's design-weighted SD, and the methods text says so | `turbotab.core.models.effects:estimand_sd` |
| implies | `the sample SD` (id `evalue-sample-sd`) | any option; when the sample answer, or no survey design | inference | the difference is standardized by the analyzed rows' own SD | `turbotab.core.models.effects:estimand_sd` |

**Primary sources:**

- VanderWeele & Ding 2017, Ann Intern Med 167:268

### An exposure family and its multiplicity (`exposure_family`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** descriptive: may read every row to say whether the data are corrupted, but informs no modeling choice. a declaration of what is reported; the tests themselves are the feature-wise family's, fit on every analyzed row, and their multiplicity is the ``multiplicity`` contract's
- **Needs:**
  - two or more exposures
- **Question:** asked within the exposure and effect question (`estimand`)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_estimand`; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 2.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference available.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the ESTIMAND package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `family`: Each exposure in turn, every member shown | customary for metabolome-wide and nutrient-wide association studies | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 1 | Sound with its multiplicity method stated; this is not selection | available, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. each exposure in turn
2. the multiplicity method
3. every member shown

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.voice:_set_estimand`.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `the family's table` (id `family-implies-multiplicity`) | any option; when an exposure family declared | inference | BH q-values or the count of tests, stated in the caption and record |  |
| implies | `the effect display` (id `family-every-member`) | any option; when an exposure family declared | inference | every member is shown, significant or not (not selection) |  |
| conflicts | `unadjusted p-values` (id `omics-unadjusted-blocked`) | any option; when an omics family | inference | blocked and recorded; exit: Benjamini–Hochberg *(rung: blocked until recorded)* |  |

**Primary sources:**

- Benjamini & Hochberg 1995, J R Stat Soc B 57:289
- Rothman 1990, Epidemiology 1:43

### Outcome-model fit statistics wait with the estimates (`fit_statistics_withheld`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself. the cross-validated scores are the outcome model's own, fit on the analyzed rows and their outcome
- **Needs:**
  - a fit under inference
- **Question:** stated
- **Where:** run by the `fit` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference recommended.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the LEASH package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `withheld`: Withheld until the plan is answered | uncommon: software reports R² beside every fit | Not offered: under prediction the scores are the result | not offered, 1 | Sound: under inference an R² describes the outcome model, not the estimate, and reading it before the plan is a fork | recommended, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. the plan open
2. estimates and fit statistics withheld
3. the plan answered
4. both shown

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.routing_leash:withheld_sentence`: What a withheld inference fit says about its scores (`estimand.SCORES_WITHHELD`).

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `no fit statistics` (id `plan-open-withholds-scores`) | any option; when under inference, a question the estimate rests on unanswered | inference | the fit serves no cross-validated R², RMSE or MAE, nor any other score | `turbotab.core.estimand:withhold` |

**Primary sources:**

- Gelman & Loken 2013 (the garden of forking paths)

### The declared model sequence (Table 2) (`model_sequence`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself. each model is fit on every analyzed row, the exposure's definition fitted once
- **Needs:**
  - a declared exposure
  - the adjustment answers
- **Question:** stated
- **Where:** recorded by `set_model_sequence`; run by the `effects` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference recommended.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the ESTIMAND package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `declared_sequence`: Unadjusted, Model 1, the primary and Model 3 | customary: the nutrition-cohort Table 2 (Westreich & Greenland 2013) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 1 | Sound when only the exposure's rows are read as effects | recommended, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. unadjusted
2. Model 1 (age, sex, energy as declared)
3. Model 2 (primary)
4. Model 3 (possible mediators)
5. the adjustment terms set apart

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.stages.effects:methods_sentence`: The methods text this stage writes, from what it fitted: the sequence, the display rule, the marginal standardization, the diagnostics and their responses, and the sensitivity analyses.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| enables | `the effect display` (id `exposure-enables-display`) | any option; when the exposure, its effect and the adjustment set answered | inference | the fit and the effects stage show estimates; withheld before |  |
| implies | `the unadjusted model` (id `crude-always`) | any option; when always | inference | the unadjusted estimate is shown (STROBE 16a) |  |
| implies | `the adjustment terms` (id `table2-appendix`) | any option; when always | inference | only the exposure's rows are effects; the rest sit under "adjustment terms, not effect estimates" |  |
| implies | `Model 3` (id `model3-labeled`) | any option; when the answers set possible mediators beside the primary | inference | Model 3 adds them, labeled as not a total effect |  |
| invalidates | `Model 1` (id `sequence-invalidated`) | any option; when another exposure, or Model 1's columns leave the primary set | inference | Model 1 is declared again, never silently kept |  |
| implies | `the analysis-plan lock` (id `sequence-in-lock`) | any option; when the plan is locked | inference | the declared sequence is part of the plan |  |
| implies | `Model 3's rows` (id `model3-own-rows`) | any option; when complete cases, and Model 3's added columns sometimes missing | inference | every other model is fit on every analyzed row (Model 2 is the fit's primary); Model 3 alone on the rows where they are recorded, the primary's adjustment refit on those rows beside it |  |
| implies | `every declared model` (id `sequence-design-based`) | any option; when the surveyed-population answer | inference | each model is design-based, or the family is blocked and recorded with the fit's exits; never an unweighted refit beside a design-based primary |  |
| disables | `the declared models` (id `sequence-supplied-copies`) | any option; when the rows are the data's own imputed copies (set_repeat_kind, kept as rows) | inference | the fit's table pools the primary over the copies; the declared models, the marginal risks, the diagnostics and the sensitivity analyses are withheld with the reason, never fit on the copies stacked |  |

**Primary sources:**

- Westreich & Greenland 2013, Am J Epidemiol 177:292
- STROBE item 16a

### The analysis-plan export (`plan_export`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** descriptive: may read every row to say whether the data are corrupted, but informs no modeling choice. a record of the decisions; reads no row
- **Needs:**
  - an inference plan
- **Question:** stated
- **Where:** recorded by `lock_plan`; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 12.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference available.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the ESTIMAND package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `export`: The plan as declared, with its SHA-256 | customary for external registration (a timestamp and a content hash) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 1 | Sound: it says what was declared in the software and when | available, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. the plan as declared
2. its canonical JSON
3. its SHA-256

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.plan_lock:plan_text`: What the export says of itself: what was declared in the software, and when; never that it was registered or specified before the data were seen (the analyst may have seen them).

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `the plan export` (id `export-replays`) | any option; when the same decision log | inference | the same bytes and the same hash |  |
| disables | `the words prespecified and preregistered` (id `never-preregistered`) | any option; when always | inference | the text says what was declared in the software and when |  |

**Primary sources:**

- Gelman & Loken 2013

### Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding (`unmeasured_confounding`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit).
- **Data scope:** descriptive: may read every row to say whether the data are corrupted, but informs no modeling choice. reads the reported estimate and, for the robustness value, the primary model's rows; informs no modeling choice
- **Needs:**
  - a reported estimate
- **Question:** stated
- **Where:** run by the `effects` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference available.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the ESTIMAND package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `robustness_value`: Robustness value, benchmarked | growing; anchored to the study's own covariates (Cinelli & Hazlett 2020) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 1 | Sound: bounded by named measured covariates; ranked first for a linear outcome | recommended, 1 |
| `e_value`: E-value | customary (growing), limited (Blum et al. 2020) | Not offered: a prediction reports no effect measure. | not offered, 2 | Conditional: no threshold exists; read against named confounders | available, 2 |

**Ranked by the data:** the app offers these options in another order than the rank above where the data decide it; what it offers first under each condition:

- Under inference, a difference from a least-squares fit (a linear outcome's coefficient): `robustness_value` then `e_value`
- Under inference, a ratio (an odds, hazard or risk ratio), or a difference with no least-squares fit: `e_value`

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. the estimate
2. how strong a confounder would have to be
3. a named measured covariate for scale

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.stages.effects:methods_sentence`: The methods text this stage writes, from what it fitted: the sequence, the display rule, the marginal standardization, the diagnostics and their responses, and the sensitivity analyses.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `every inference result` (id `sensitivity-offered`) | any option; when an estimate is reported | inference | its sensitivity analysis is shown |  |
| implies | `the order of the analyses` (id `rv-first-linear`) | any option; when a linear outcome | inference | the robustness value leads, the E-value follows |  |
| disables | `a pass/fail verdict` (id `no-threshold`) | any option; when always | inference | no E-value or robustness value is called a pass or a fail |  |
| disables | `the robustness value's interval form` (id `rv-interval-classical`) | any option; when the interval shown is not the classical one (HC3, cluster-robust, pooled) | inference | RV for the interval and the benchmarks' intervals are not reported, and the reading says why; RV_q and the adjusted estimates stay |  |
| implies | `the straight-line estimate` (id `curve-straight-line`) | any option; when the exposure enters as a curve (a spline) | inference | its straight-line estimate beside it is shown and bounded, and named so |  |

**Primary sources:**

- VanderWeele & Ding 2017, Ann Intern Med 167:268
- Cinelli & Hazlett 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:39

### Model explanations (`explain`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 1.
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself.
- **Needs:**
  - a fitted family that predicts
  - the rows it was fit on
  - its cross-validated score against the no-predictor baseline
  - under inference, the declared exposure
- **Question:** How should the fitted models be described?
- **Where:** recorded by `set_explain`; run by the `explain` stage.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the EXPLAIN package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ale`: Accumulated local effects | Less used in applied papers than partial dependence (Apley & Zhu 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:1059–1086). | Sound with correlated intakes: it averages local changes among rows that hold such values (Apley & Zhu 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:1059–1086). | recommended, 1 | Describes the fitted model beside the declared estimate; it is not an effect estimate. | recommended, 1 |
| `partial_dependence`: Partial dependence | The usual curve in applied machine-learning papers (Friedman 2001, Ann Stat 29:1189–1232). | Averages predictions over every row's other values, including intake combinations the data never hold when intakes are correlated (Apley & Zhu 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:1059–1086; Molnar et al. 2022, xxAI, LNCS 13200:39–68: "ignoring feature dependencies"). | ranked lower, concern stated, 2 | Averages predictions over every row's other values, including intake combinations the data never hold when intakes are correlated (Apley & Zhu 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:1059–1086; Molnar et al. 2022, xxAI, LNCS 13200:39–68: "ignoring feature dependencies"). | ranked lower, concern stated, 2 |
| `as_effect`: Report the explanations as each exposure's effect | Common enough to be a named pitfall (Molnar et al. 2022, xxAI, LNCS 13200:39–68: "making unjustified causal interpretations"). | A prediction model's explanations describe its predictions; an effect needs a declared exposure and effect under inference. | refused, with an exit, 3 | The effect is the declared estimand's estimate; an explanation of a fitted model is not an effect estimate. | refused, with an exit, 3 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. Each family fit on the same rows
2. Each prediction split into its inputs' SHAP values
3. Refit on resamples, for stability
4. Pairs ranked by their interaction
5. Each exposure's curve per family, where it beats the baseline

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.models.explain:methods_sentence`: The methods paragraph the explanations write, from what was computed: it names only the families and inputs a curve was drawn for, and says which families drew none and why.
- Its clause in a chain's methods paragraph (`contracts.paragraph`) is written by `a function in turbotab.core.models.explain`.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `performance_floor` | any option | prediction | A family whose cross-validated score does not beat the no-predictor baseline draws no curve, and says why. |  |
| implies | `unit_resampling` | any option | prediction, inference | Rows that repeat within a unit are resampled as whole units in the refits that measure stability. |  |
| implies | `domain_transform` | any option | prediction, inference | Each curve is drawn on the exposure's final scale, as the model reads it after energy adjustment or normalization, the scale its form is declared on. |  |
| conflicts | `effect_estimate` | `as_effect` | prediction, inference | An explanation describes a fitted model's predictions, not what changing an intake would do, so it is never reported as an effect. *(rung: refused, with an exit)* |  |
| implies | `plan_lock` | any option | inference | Under inference the explanations wait until the exposure, its effect and the adjustment set are answered, and their first display locks the analysis plan. |  |
| implies | `adjustment_terms` | any option | inference | Under inference the covariates' attributions are labeled adjustment terms, not effect estimates. |  |
| implies | `multiple_imputation` | any option | inference | Under multiple imputation the explanations describe the model fitted on one in-fold fill and estimate nothing. |  |

**Primary sources:**

- Lundberg & Lee 2017, NeurIPS 30:4765–4774
- Lundberg et al. 2020, Nat Mach Intell 2:56–67
- Friedman & Popescu 2008, Ann Appl Stat 2:916–954
- Apley & Zhu 2020, J R Stat Soc B 82:1059–1086
- Friedman 2001, Ann Stat 29:1189–1232
- Molnar et al. 2022, xxAI, LNCS 13200:39–68

### Multiplicity control (`multiplicity`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 1.
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself.
- **Needs:**
  - an exposure family
- **Question:** The exposures are tested as a family: how is multiplicity controlled?
- **Where:** recorded by `set_multiplicity` (the contract does not name it).
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared).

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bh`: Benjamini–Hochberg q-values | Customary for MWAS and EWAS | Sound: holds the false-discovery rate (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995). | recommended, 1 | Sound: holds the false-discovery rate (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995). | recommended, 1 |
| `stated_count`: Number of tests stated | Customary for a few hypotheses (Rothman 1990) | Sound for a few prespecified hypotheses only. | blocked until recorded, 2 | Sound for a few prespecified hypotheses only. | blocked until recorded, 2 |
| `none`: No control | Not customary | Unsound for a family. | blocked until recorded, 3 | Unsound for a family. | blocked until recorded, 3 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. Test each exposure on its own
2. Adjust the p-values across the family

**Methods sentence:**

- **None declared:** no template, no sentence function, no clause and no in-fold phrase.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `bh_q_values` | any option | inference | An exposure family implies multiplicity control: BH q-values for feature-wise analyses; every member is shown. |  |
| conflicts | `unadjusted_family` | any option | inference | A feature-wise table without multiplicity control is blocked and recorded. *(rung: blocked until recorded)* |  |

**Primary sources:**

- Benjamini & Hochberg 1995
- Rothman 1990
- Gelman & Loken 2013

### A strictly proper primary score (`proper_primary`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 1.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each score reads the out-of-fold or out-of-resample predictions of models fit on the training rows only; nothing here is learned from a row it scores.
- **Needs:**
  - the task
  - out-of-fold predictions
- **Question:** (stated, not asked: the primary score is strictly proper)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_split`; run by the `fit` stage; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the VALID package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `proper`: A strictly proper per-row loss | AUC and the C-index are the field's customary headline (semi-proper) | Stated, not asked: compare, choose and declare on the primary; the customary headline reported beside it with the tension | recommended, 1 | Stated: the scores describe fit, not the estimate | available, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. score each row's prediction by a per-row proper loss
2. average the losses
3. report AUC or C beside it as the customary headline

**Methods sentence:**

- Template: “{headline} is the customary headline: it ranks risks without asking whether they are right (semi-proper), so the models were compared, chosen and declared on {primary}, a strictly proper score (Van Calster et al., STRATOS TG6).”

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `customary_headline` (id `proper_score_primary`) | any option; when a binary, ordinal or time-to-event task | prediction, inference | the comparisons, the choice and the declaration read the strictly proper primary; AUC or C is reported as the customary headline | `turbotab.core.models.metrics:tension` |

**Primary sources:**

- Van Calster et al., STRATOS TG6, arXiv:2412.10288
- Harrell, Statistically efficient ways to quantify added predictive value

### The substitution curve over the surveyed population (`survey_substitution`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 1.
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself. The weighted fit learns from the outcome and every study row in its domain (the analysis rows); the strata and PSUs enter only its variance. Lockbox §06's test: row i's fitted value moves with the outcome.
- **Needs:**
  - the survey answer: the surveyed population (a weight, and strata and PSUs)
  - a substitution answer
  - the linear family chosen
- **Question:** Which energy substitution, in what steps? (the substitution question)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_substitution`; run by the `substitution` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 11's displays, beside the coefficient table.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction not offered; inference recommended.
- **Lenses:** Dietary assessment. Declared by the SURVEY package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design_band`: A band by Taylor linearization over the survey design | Predictive margins with survey data (Graubard & Korn 1999) | Not asked: under prediction the scores describe the rows they were computed on, and the weights are noted, not used. | not offered, 2 | Sound for the surveyed population: the band carries both the error of the weighted fit and which people were sampled. | recommended, 1 |
| `row_bootstrap`: A band from refits on bootstrap resamples of rows | The band this app draws without a survey design | The band prediction draws on its training rows. | recommended, 1 | Not under the population answer: a row bootstrap ignores the strata and PSUs, so the design's band replaces it. | not offered, 2 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. Refit the linear family with the weights
2. Move k kcal on every row on support
3. Average each row's change over the population (weighted)
4. Linearize the average over the design for its band

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.models.survey:substitution_clause`: The `set_substitution` sentence's clause under the population answer (the curve's contract sentence), or None. `n_boot`: the bootstrap refits the answer asked for, which the design's band replaces and the clause says are not drawn. `per_class`: a multiclass outcome's curves, one per class (`methods.substitution.class_clause`).
- Its clause in a chain's methods paragraph (`contracts.paragraph`) is written by `turbotab.core.models.survey:_substitution_contract_clause`.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| invalidates | `the substitution band from row resampling` (id `bootstrap_band`) | any option | inference | A row bootstrap ignores the strata and PSUs, so the band is the design's instead. | `turbotab.core.models.survey:design_curve` |
| conflicts | `a curve from a family with no design-based estimator` (id `blocked_curve`) | any option | inference | Blocked and recorded: no curve, its reason and its exits. *(rung: blocked until recorded)* Exits: the design-based family in its place, every other chosen family kept; the sample-only attestation. | `turbotab.core.models.survey:population_curve` |

**Primary sources:**

- Graubard & Korn 1999, Biometrics 55:652
- R survey::svyglm + svycontrast

### Repeated k-fold comparison substrate (`comparison_substrate`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 2.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each score reads the out-of-fold or out-of-resample predictions of models fit on the training rows only; nothing here is learned from a row it scores.
- **Needs:**
  - training rows
  - the unit when rows repeat
- **Question:** (stated: whatever validation leads, at least 10 × K folds)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_split`; run by the `fit` stage; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the VALID package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repeated_kfold`: At least 10 × K folds, whole units together | A single k-fold run or one split is the field's habit | Stated: whatever validation leads, at least 10 × K folds | recommended, 1 | Not a comparison | not offered, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. draw the folds 10 times, whole units together
2. fit every family and the baseline on each fold
3. pair their fold scores
4. the corrected repeated k-fold t

- Template: “models were compared with each other and with the no-predictor baseline on {folds}-fold cross-validation repeated {repeats} times, by the corrected repeated k-fold t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004)”

| implies | `grouped_resampling` (id `repeated_units_group_resampling`) | any option; when rows repeat within a unit | prediction, inference | grouped folds in every repeat, a grouped holdout, a bootstrap by unit, BBC-CV by unit and nested folds by unit | `turbotab.core.models.folds:kfold_assignment` |

| implies | `site_heterogeneity` (id `clusters_site_heterogeneity`) | any option; when the grouping question named a column with 2 to 30 levels | prediction | every family is also validated internal–externally by the grouping, each level scored by models fit on the others, with the random-effects summary and the spread (TRIPOD+AI 12d, 23b) | `turbotab.core.models.validation:internal_external` |

### Substitution curves for a multiclass outcome, one per class (`multiclass_substitution`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 2.
- **Data scope:** model: the outcome model itself. Each curve follows the fitted outcome model, so a row's predicted change moves with the outcome and with every row the model was fit on. Lockbox §06's test: row i's change in each class's probability moves when the outcome does.
- **Needs:**
  - a multiclass outcome (three or more unordered classes)
  - two energy-bearing exposures whose kcal per unit is settled
  - a fitted family that predicts each class's probability
  - the substitution answer (donor, recipient and step)
- **Question:** Which energy substitution, in what steps? (the substitution question; a multiclass outcome draws one curve per class)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_substitution`; run by the `substitution` stage; placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 11's displays: beside the coefficient table under inference, beside the comparison under prediction.
- **The method's own leash:** prediction recommended; inference recommended.
- **Lenses:** Dietary assessment. Declared by the MULTISUB package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `class_curves`: One curve per class: the average change in each class's predicted probability | Average discrete changes of a multinomial model on each outcome's probability (Long & Freese 2014, ch. 8; Stata margins and R marginaleffects per outcome) | Sound as a model contrast: what the fitted model predicts for each class when k kcal move. | recommended, 1 | Sound: a marginal, isocaloric contrast on the probability scale over the stated population; the curves sum to zero at every k, as each person's probabilities sum to one. | recommended, 1 |
| `reference_ratios`: Relative-risk ratios against the reference class per kcal swapped | The multinomial coefficients' contrast, as categorical-outcome analyses report them | Not a prediction: the class curves say what the model predicts. | not offered, 2 | Conditional on every covariate and against one reference class: it says how the odds of a class against the reference move, not how any class's probability does, and it is one number only when every energy source is a linear term. The coefficient table reports each class's ratios per unit. | not offered, 2 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. Predict every class's probability on every row
2. Move k kcal from the donor to the recipient on every row on support
3. Predict again, and take each class's change
4. Average each class's change over the same rows (weighted under a surveyed population)
5. Check that the class curves sum to zero at every k
6. Band each class: refits on bootstrap resamples, Rubin's rules over the imputations, or the survey design's linearization

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:class_clause`: The `set_substitution` sentence's clause for a multiclass outcome (its contract's sentence), or None. It reads the recorded task only, so the methods text restates it whole.
- Its clause in a chain's methods paragraph (`contracts.paragraph`) is written by `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:_contract_clause`.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `class_probabilities_sum_to_one` (id `curves_sum_to_zero`) | any option | prediction, inference | The class curves sum to zero at every k, because each row's class probabilities sum to one before and after the move; a set that does not is a defect, raised and never drawn. | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:check_sums_to_zero` |
| implies | `refit_band` | any option; when a band asked for (n_boot > 0) with no surveyed population | prediction, inference | Each class's band comes from refits of the model on bootstrap resamples of the rows it was fit on (whole units when rows repeat), its interval read from that class's refits. | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:class_refit_band` |
| implies | `multiple_imputation_compatible` (id `pooled_per_k`) | any option; when multiple imputation under inference | inference | Each completed copy's class curves are drawn on that copy's rows through that copy's own fit (a family with no coefficient table refit on each copy), and pooled at each k by Rubin's rules; a curve from one fill is never shown. | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:pool_class_curves` |
| conflicts | `imputation_blocked` (id `blocked_with_the_table`) | any option; when multiple imputation under inference with blanks among the analyzed rows, blocked and recorded or with no copies drawn | inference | While the missing-values answer blocks the coefficient table under inference (passive imputation with a declared nonlinear term, single-level imputation on clustered rows, imputation that cannot run on these data), or no imputed copies were drawn for the fit, no class curve is drawn: each family's curves are blocked and recorded with the table's own refusal and exits, never drawn on one fill of the blanks. *(rung: blocked until recorded)* Exits: the coefficient table's own exits (complete cases, with their assumption stated, among them); with no copies drawn: the linear model added, whose coefficient table draws them. | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:missing_values_block` |
| implies | `survey_population` (id `design_based`) | any option; when the survey answer "the surveyed population" | inference | Each class's curve comes from the survey-weighted multinomial fit, averaged with the weights, and its band is Taylor linearization over the survey design; refits on bootstrap resamples of rows are not drawn. | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:design_class_curves` |
| conflicts | `survey_population` (id `blocked_family`) | any option; when the survey answer "the surveyed population" and a family with no design-based estimator | inference | A family with no design-based estimator draws no class curves under the surveyed population: blocked and recorded. *(rung: blocked until recorded)* Exits: the design-based family in its place, every other chosen family kept; the sample-only attestation. | `turbotab.core.stages.class_substitution:population_blocked` |
| conflicts | `survey_population` (id `no_design_df`) | any option; when the survey answer "the surveyed population" with no design degrees of freedom (every PSU alone in its stratum) | inference | A design whose analysis rows lie in no more PSUs than strata leaves no degrees of freedom for an interval: the coefficient table is refused, and no class curve is drawn either, blocked and recorded, never shown as points under a caption that promises intervals. *(rung: blocked until recorded)* Exits: the sample-only attestation. | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:no_design_df` |
| conflicts | `omitted_energy_sources` (id `omitted_sources`) | any option; when energy sources left out above MAX_OMITTED_SHARE of total energy | inference | Energy sources left out of the model, above the stated share of total energy, block the swap under inference until it is recorded: the curves carry the confounding of the sources total energy holds as one composite. *(rung: blocked until recorded)* Exits: add each missing energy source to the model as an exposure; Keep this swap; the curve carries their confounding; Choose another swap. | `turbotab.core.decisions:_substitution_has_every_energy_source` |
| implies | `omitted_energy_sources` (id `omitted_stated`) | any option; when energy sources left out of the model | prediction | Under prediction the curves are model contrasts: the sources the model leaves out are named as a concern, never blocked. | `turbotab.core.methods.energy:omitted_sentence` |
| implies | `estimand_label` | any option | prediction, inference | The estimand names the probability scale, the isocaloric move and the population the curves average over; each class's label is the change in its probability at the stated k, an average over that population, since a multinomial model's change depends on k and on each person's intake (MODELING_SEQUENCE §2). | `turbotab.core.methods.substitution:class_estimand` |

**Primary sources:**

- Long & Freese 2014, Regression Models for Categorical Dependent Variables Using Stata, 3rd ed., ch. 8
- Graubard & Korn 1999, Biometrics 55:652
- Rubin 1987, Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys
- Tomova, Gilthorpe & Tennant 2022 (substitution models; PMC9630885)
- MODELING_SEQUENCE §2, §4

### Bootstrap bias-corrected cross-validation (`bbc_cv`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 3.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each score reads the out-of-fold or out-of-resample predictions of models fit on the training rows only; nothing here is learned from a row it scores.
- **Needs:**
  - two or more families
  - their out-of-fold predictions
- **Question:** (stated: the choice among families is corrected)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_split`; run by the `fit` stage; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the VALID package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bbc_cv`: The choice corrected by BBC-CV | Reporting the best family's own cross-validated score is the field's habit | Stated: the choice among families is corrected; with no holdout the selection-corrected estimate is the result (refuse the winner's own score as the result) | recommended, 1 | Not applicable | not offered, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. resample the out-of-fold predictions by unit
2. choose the best family on the resample
3. score it on the units left out
4. average

**Methods sentence:**

- Template: “the choice among {k} families was corrected by bootstrap bias-corrected cross-validation (Tsamardinos et al. 2018, {b} resamples)”

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `selection_corrected_score` (id `choice_among_families_bbc`) | any option; when two or more families under prediction | prediction | the best family's score is corrected for the choice | `turbotab.core.models.selection:selection_optimism` |
| conflicts | `winner_own_score` (id `no_holdout_declares_corrected`) | any option; when no rows held out and the families compared | prediction | the winner's own score as the result is refused; the selection-corrected estimate is the result *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: Keep the compared families. | `turbotab.core.models.selection:_compared_families_stay` |

**Primary sources:**

- Tsamardinos, Greasidou & Borboudakis, Mach Learn 2018;107:1895

### Bootstrap optimism correction (`bootstrap_optimism`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 4.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each score reads the out-of-fold or out-of-resample predictions of models fit on the training rows only; nothing here is learned from a row it scores.
- **Needs:**
  - a regression-type family
  - the whole pipeline
- **Question:** How is performance estimated on these rows?
- **Where:** recorded by `set_split`; run by the `fit` stage; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the VALID package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bootstrap`: Harrell's bootstrap, the whole pipeline refit on each resample | Steyerberg's floor of 200 resamples is customary | Asked (the split question), ranked first below 20,000 units; at least 500 resamples (Collins et al. 2024) | recommended, 1 | Offered after one cross-validation run | available, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. fit on every row: the apparent score
2. refit on a resample of whole units
3. score it on the resample and on every row
4. average the gap: the optimism
5. subtract it

**Methods sentence:**

- Template: “Harrell's bootstrap ({b} resamples, the whole pipeline refit on each)”

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `resample_concern` (id `bootstrap_resamples`) | any option; when fewer than 500 resamples | prediction, inference | the concern is stated (Collins et al. 2024) | `turbotab.core.models.validation:resample_concern` |

**Primary sources:**

- Harrell, Lee & Mark, Stat Med 1996;15:361
- Collins et al., BMJ 2024;384:e074819

### Calibration by a horizon, and by level (`horizon_calibration`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 5.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each score reads the out-of-fold or out-of-resample predictions of models fit on the training rows only; nothing here is learned from a row it scores.
- **Needs:**
  - a time to event with its follow-up and a horizon
  - or an ordinal or multiclass outcome
- **Question:** (stated: the prediction horizon is declared with the follow-up, else the median follow-up time)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_split`; run by the `fit` stage; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the VALID package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `by_horizon_and_level`: At the horizon; by level for ordinal and multiclass outcomes | Calibration is often left unreported for these tasks | Stated: the prediction horizon is declared with the follow-up, else the median follow-up time | recommended, 1 | Stated beside the fit scores | available, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. each row's risk by the horizon
2. the Kaplan–Meier observed risk
3. observed against expected, by risk group
4. the calibration slope

**Methods sentence:**

- Template: “calibration was assessed at {horizon} by observed (Kaplan–Meier) against predicted risk and the calibration slope”

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| implies | `not_assessed_note` (id `calibration_not_assessed`) | any option; when calibration cannot be computed | prediction, inference | the record says calibration not assessed, and why | `turbotab.core.models.validation:calibration_by` |

**Primary sources:**

- Graf et al., Stat Med 1999;18:2529

### The nested cross-validation interval (`nested_cv_interval`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 6.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each score reads the out-of-fold or out-of-resample predictions of models fit on the training rows only; nothing here is learned from a row it scores.
- **Needs:**
  - a per-row proper loss
  - p ≫ n
- **Question:** Predictors outnumber the rows: run the nested cross-validation interval?
- **Where:** recorded by `set_split`; run by the `fit` stage; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the VALID package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nested_cv`: Bates, Hastie & Tibshirani's nested cross-validation interval | The naive cross-validation interval is customary | Offered with its compute estimate where p/n > 1; else the interval is labeled likely too narrow | available, 1 | Not applicable | not offered, 1 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. for each repetition, each pair of folds fit without both
2. each fold fit without it
3. the spread of the inner against the outer errors
4. widen the interval by it

**Methods sentence:**

- Template: “each family's own performance interval is the nested cross-validation interval ({reps} repetitions of {folds} folds; Bates, Hastie & Tibshirani 2023)”

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| enables | `nested_cv_interval` (id `p_much_greater_n`) | any option; when more candidate predictors than rows | prediction | the nested cross-validation interval is offered for each family's own score, and the naive interval is labeled likely too narrow until it runs; the selection-corrected interval keeps the label, since no nested interval exists for a choice among families | `turbotab.core.models.validation:nested_cv_interval` |

**Primary sources:**

- Bates, Hastie & Tibshirani, JASA 2023 (arXiv:2104.00673)

### Leave-one-site-out validation, pooled across sites (`site_validation`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 6.5.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. Each held-out site is scored by a pipeline made fresh and fitted on the other sites' rows only, so everything learned is learned inside the training fold; the pooling reads only the sites' scores.
- **Needs:**
  - a declared site, cluster or batch column with at least three levels
  - a numeric or yes/no outcome
  - the whole pipeline, refitted per site
  - optional: the unit when rows repeat (each in one site)
- **Question:** (stated: REML random effects with the Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman interval)
- **Where:** recorded by `set_validation`; placed at 11 · Tuning and comparison.
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the SITEVAL package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reml_hksj`: REML random effects, Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman interval | Snell et al. 2018 (REML, HKSJ, logit C); metafor's rma (Viechtbauer 2010) | Sound with few sites: the interval allows for τ² being estimated; the prediction interval says where a new site would land | recommended, 1 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: it validates a prediction model at a site it never saw | not offered, 1 |
| `dl_wald`: DerSimonian–Laird random effects, Wald interval | The customary random-effects summary; the fit's own internal–external summary | Sound with many sites; with few, its interval is too narrow | available, 2 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: it validates a prediction model at a site it never saw | not offered, 2 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. hold one site out
2. fit the whole pipeline on the other sites
3. score the held-out site: C statistic, calibration-in-the-large, slope
4. repeat for every site
5. pool the sites, with the prediction interval and I²

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:site_validation_sentence`: The methods sentence of leave-one-site-out validation.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| implies | `fitted_in_fold` (id `in_fold`) | any option; when always | prediction | the pipeline is made fresh for each held-out site and fitted on the other sites only | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:site_validation` |
| implies | `logit_c_scale` (id `pooling_scales`) | any option; when a yes/no outcome | prediction | the C statistic is pooled on the logit scale and transformed back; the calibration measures on their own | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:pool` |
| implies | `prediction_interval` (id `new_site_interval`) | any option; when three or more sites scored | prediction | each pooled measure carries a 95% prediction interval for a new site, said before I² | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:pool` |
| implies | `unscored_site_listed` (id `unscored_site`) | any option; when a site that cannot be scored | prediction | a site with one outcome class only, or too few rows, or a C statistic of exactly 0 or 1, is listed with its reason and left out of that measure's pooling, the pooled note naming it | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:site_validation` |
| implies | `clustered_site_intervals` (id `clustered_sites`) | any option; when rows repeat within a unit | prediction | each site's intervals are clustered by the unit | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:site_validation` |
| conflicts | `too_few_sites` (id `min_sites`) | any option; when fewer than three sites | prediction | refused with fewer than three sites *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: k-fold cross-validation. | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:site_validation` |
| conflicts | `unit_in_two_sites` (id `unit_across_sites`) | any option; when a unit in more than one site | prediction | refused when a unit's rows lie in more than one site *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: correct the site column; k-fold cross-validation. | `turbotab.core.methods.site_validation:site_validation` |

### Intended use, the decision curve and the threshold (`intended_use`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 7.
- **Data scope:** training fold: learns from study rows, so it is fit in-fold. The curve reads the out-of-fold predictions, and a named threshold is chosen on each training fold and scored on the fold its model never saw.
- **Needs:**
  - a yes/no outcome
  - out-of-fold predictions
- **Question:** Will the model support a decision at a risk threshold?
- **Where:** recorded by `set_intended_use`; run by the `evaluation` stage; placed at 2 · Exposure and estimand (prediction: intended use).
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the EXPLORE package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decision_support`: Decision support: the decision curve, a threshold chosen in-fold | Decision curves are recommended but still rare in nutrition papers | Sound: net benefit over the declared threshold range (Vickers & Elkin 2006; STRATOS TG6 lists it as essential) | recommended, 1 | Not asked: no score is reported under inference | not offered, 1 |
| `risk_estimation`: Risk estimation only: no threshold | Most prediction papers report discrimination and calibration only | Sound when no decision rests on a cut-off; the curve is not drawn | available, 2 | Not asked: no score is reported under inference | not offered, 2 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. each row's out-of-fold risk
2. count true and false positives at each threshold
3. weigh false positives by the threshold's odds
4. against treating everyone and no one

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.models.decision_curve:intended_use_sentence`: The `set_intended_use` record's sentence.

| implies | `threshold_in_fold` (id `threshold_chosen_in_fold`) | `decision_support`; when decision support | prediction | a named threshold is chosen in each training fold and scored on the fold its model never saw | `turbotab.core.models.decision_curve:threshold_in_fold` |
| implies | `subgroup_performance` (id `subgroups_scored`) | any option; when subgroup columns named | prediction | performance with intervals in each named sociodemographic subgroup (TRIPOD+AI 23a), the fairness approach recorded (item 14) | `turbotab.core.models.decision_curve:subgroup_performance` |
| implies | `code_or_count_reading` (id `subgroups_read_the_ledger`) | any option; when subgroup columns named | prediction | each named column's groups are its levels when its numbers are codes and its thirds when they are an amount, as its settled reading says; while it is unsettled the column is asked, never grouped by its count of values | `turbotab.core.models.decision_curve:grouping_of` |
| enables | `model_updating` (id `shrinkage_offered`) | any option; when an unpenalized regression family | prediction | uniform shrinkage by the calibration slope is offered as model updating | `turbotab.core.models.decision_curve:shrinkage` |

### Agreement between two measurements (Bland–Altman) (`bland_altman`)

- **Slot:** evaluation (after the fit); place in it 8.
- **Data scope:** descriptive: may read every row to say whether the data are corrupted, but informs no modeling choice. Nothing is fitted per fold. It reads every analyzed pair (under Describe, every eligible row, as an estimate does) and never the outcome model; under Predict it reads the two models' out-of-fold predictions only. It reports, and nothing it computes is applied to a row or informs a modeling choice.
- **Needs:**
  - two numeric measurements of the same quantity on the same rows (two columns), or two fitted models' out-of-fold predictions of a numeric or yes/no outcome
  - at least three complete pairs
  - optional: the person each pair belongs to (repeated pairs), the survey design
- **Question:** How closely do the two measurements agree?
- **Lenses:** every lens (shared). Declared by the AGREEMENT package.

**Options**, each labeled customary and sound for each purpose, with its leash rung and its rank (1 is offered first):

| Option | Customary | Sound for prediction | Rung, rank (prediction) | Sound for inference | Rung, rank (inference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `differences`: Differences: bias and 95% limits of agreement | The standard method-comparison analysis (Bland & Altman 1986, 1999); BlandAltmanLeh and blandr in R | Sound for two models' out-of-fold predictions of a number; describes how far apart they are, not which is right | available, 1 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: agreement describes two measurements and is not an effect (offered under Describe; see DESCRIBE_LABELS) | not offered, 1 |
| `ratios`: Ratios: the analysis on the log scale, back-transformed | Bland & Altman 1986 for a spread that grows with the size | Sound when both models' predictions are above zero and their gap grows with the size; refused with a value at or below zero | available, 2 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: agreement describes two measurements and is not an effect (offered under Describe; see DESCRIBE_LABELS) | not offered, 2 |
| `regression`: Regression-based limits of agreement | Bland & Altman 1999; less common in published comparisons | Sound when the gap changes with the size; one pair per row only | available, 3 | Not offered under Estimate an effect: agreement describes two measurements and is not an effect (offered under Describe; see DESCRIBE_LABELS) | not offered, 3 |

**Storyboard** (the transform player's real steps):

1. pair each row's two values
2. take the difference (or the log ratio) and the pair's mean
3. the bias: the mean difference, with its interval
4. the limits: bias ± 1.96 SD, with their intervals
5. check the difference and its spread against the mean

**Methods sentence:**

- Written by `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement_sentence`: The methods sentence of a Bland–Altman agreement analysis, naming its form, its intervals, its checks and any weighting or repeated pairs.

**Relations:**

| Kind | Toward | Fires for | Purposes | What the app says | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| conflicts | `ratios_need_positive_values` (id `ratios_need_positive`) | `ratios`; when a value at or below zero | describe, prediction | ratios are refused when a value is zero or below *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: the differences; the regression-based limits. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| implies | `spread_noticed` (id `spread_grows`) | `differences`; when the absolute residual's slope on the mean above zero at p < 0.05 | describe, prediction | a spread that grows with the size is noticed, and the ratios form (all values above zero) or the regression-based limits are offered first | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| implies | `proportional_bias_reported` (id `proportional_bias`) | any option; when always | describe, prediction | the slope of the difference on the pair's mean is reported with its interval | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| implies | `repeated_pairs_components` (id `repeated_pairs`) | `differences`, `ratios`; when a person with more than one pair | describe, prediction | the SD of a difference combines the between- and within-person variance (Bland & Altman 2007), with MOVER intervals (Zou 2013), and the slopes are clustered by person | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| conflicts | `regression_limits_need_one_pair` (id `regression_one_pair`) | `regression`; when a person with more than one pair | describe, prediction | regression-based limits are refused with repeated pairs per person *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: the differences; the ratios; one pair per person. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| implies | `population_design` (id `design_based`) | any option; when a survey design answered as the surveyed population (Describe) | describe | the bias, the limits and the slopes are weighted, with design-based standard errors on t(PSUs − strata) | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| conflicts | `repeated_pairs_under_design` (id `repeats_not_weighted`) | any option; when the surveyed population and a person with more than one pair | describe | repeated pairs per person under the population answer are refused: the variance-components form has no design-based version in common use *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: one pair per person; the sample-only attestation. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| conflicts | `no_design_df` (id `design_df`) | any option; when the pairs lie in as many PSUs as strata | describe | no design degrees of freedom are left for an interval *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: the sample-only attestation. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:agreement` |
| implies | `out_of_fold_only` (id `out_of_fold`) | any option; when two fitted models | prediction | two models are compared on their out-of-fold predictions only; a row no fold scored is left out | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:model_agreement` |
| conflicts | `one_number_per_row` (id `one_number`) | any option; when a multiclass or time-to-event outcome | prediction | refused for a multiclass or time-to-event outcome: their predictions are not one number per row *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: compare the models by their scores. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:model_agreement` |
| conflicts | `not_an_effect` (id `estimate_refused`) | any option; when the Estimate an effect goal | inference | not offered under Estimate an effect: agreement is a description *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: ask it under Describe. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:eligible` |
| conflicts | `methods_are_described` (id `methods_under_predict`) | any option; when two measurement columns under Predict | prediction | two measurement methods are compared under Describe, not Predict *(rung: refused, with an exit)* Exits: ask it under Describe. | `turbotab.core.methods.agreement:eligible` |

- Bland & Altman 1986, Lancet i:307 (doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(86)90837-8)

- Bland & Altman 2007, J Biopharm Stat 17:571 (doi:10.1080/10543400701329422)
